title: k-fold CRT, Pi-type form: ℤ/(∏ nᵢ)ℤ ≅ ∏_{i:Fin k} ℤ/nᵢℤ

problemStatement.formal:
**Theorem (crtPi)**: For a pairwise-coprime family ns : Fin k → ℕ (i ≠ j ⟹ Coprime (ns i) (ns j)),
  ZMod (∏ i, ns i) ≃+* ∀ i : Fin k, ZMod (ns i)
as rings, indexed symmetrically by Fin k.
problemStatement.plain: The k-fold Chinese Remainder Theorem in its canonical dependent-product (Pi-type) form, indexed symmetrically by Fin k. For a pairwise-coprime family ns : Fin k → ℕ, the ring ZMod (∏ i, ns i) is isomorphic to the dependent product ∀ i : Fin k, ZMod (ns i). This answers the third open question of the parent k-fold CRT entry, which proved the list/nested-pair form ZMod ns.prod ≃+* CRTProd ns with a right-associated PUnit tower. The Pi-type form is the standard textbook statement and is reusable as an indexed product (no nested pairs). Constructed directly by induction on k: the base case uses that ZMod 1 and the empty Pi-type are both subsingletons; the step splits off the head ns 0 via Fin.prod_univ_succ, applies the binary ZMod.chineseRemainder with head-coprime-to-tail-product, recurses, and reassembles with a Fin.cons ring isomorphism. Includes bijectivity, ring-hom properties, a round-trip identity, the cardinality consequence |∏ᵢ ZMod nᵢ| = ∏ nᵢ, and a concrete ℤ/30ℤ ≅ ∏ ℤ/[2,3,5]ᵢℤ example.

finSplitRingEquiv: the Fin.cons ring isomorphism (∀ i : Fin (k+1), M i) ≃+* M 0 × (∀ i : Fin k, M i.succ), with map_mul'/map_add' true by rfl

insights: Indexing by Fin k (not a List) gives the symmetric, reusable product form — the standard CRT statement — at the cost of a Fin.cons reassembly step

finSplitRingEquiv is a ring isomorphism whose map_mul'/map_add' are literally rfl: products and sums on dependent function types are pointwise, so splitting off the head commutes with the ring operations definitionally
The k = 0 base avoids ZMod (∏ Fin 0) ≠ ZMod 1 friction by rewriting the empty product to 1 and invoking a generic subsingleton ring isomorphism
head_coprime_tail_prod packages Nat.Coprime.prod_right: the head is coprime to every tail factor (each indexed by i.succ ≠ 0), hence to their product
Cardinality preservation is a free corollary: a ring bijection transports Nat.card, and Nat.card (ZMod N) = N for N ≠ 0, giving ∏ᵢ |ZMod nᵢ| = ∏ nᵢ
Example coprimality is discharged by kernel `decide`, keeping the entry axiom-free (no native_decide / Lean.ofReduceBool)
